bib.title: Natural Adversarial Examples
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v4, 4 Mar 2021; CVPR 2021 per common citation, not printed)

question: Can real, unmodified images be adversarially filtered so that they reliably degrade many unseen ImageNet classifiers and OOD detectors, and what helps?
hypothesis: Adversarially filtered natural images selected against ResNet-50 will transfer to other architectures, exposing shared weaknesses that augmentation and extra data barely fix.
contributions: ImageNet-A: 7,500 adversarially filtered images over 200 ImageNet classes
ImageNet-O: 2,000 adversarially filtered OOD images, first OOD dataset for ImageNet models
Evidence that augmentation and extra data help little while architecture changes help more
Shows examples transfer across CNNs and vision transformers

method.summary: Images scraped from iNaturalist, Flickr and DuckDuckGo are kept only if ResNet-50 filters misclassify them with low confidence, then hand-selected. ImageNet-O uses ImageNet-22K images outside ImageNet-1K classes that ResNet-50 labels with high confidence. Many models are then evaluated on both sets.
method.task: image classification robustness and out-of-distribution detection benchmark

datasets.name: ImageNet-A
datasets.split: test only (one run fine-tunes on 80% and tests on 20%)
datasets.source: iNaturalist, Flickr, DuckDuckGo; hand-selected by graduate students over several months
datasets.preprocessing: removed if any of 10 crops of either ResNet-50 is correct or correct-class confidence >15%; at most 15 per confusion pair in shortlist; manual selection

datasets.name: ImageNet-O
datasets.split: test only; in-distribution scores from ImageNet validation of the same 200 classes
datasets.preprocessing: kept images ResNet-50 classifies with high confidence

models.name: ResNet-50 (two filter models)
models.architecture: ResNet-50; one pretrained on ImageNet-1K then fine-tuned on 200 classes, one with 200 of 1,000 logits

models.name: AlexNet, SqueezeNet, VGG, DenseNet, ResNet/ResNeXt/SE/Res2Net/DPN, DeiT-tiny/small/base

inference.samples: not stated (single numbers reported, no seeds or error bars)

metrics.name: AUPR on ImageNet-O
metrics.definition: area under precision-recall curve, anomaly score = negative MSP, ImageNet val of 200 classes as in-distribution

metrics.name: AURRA
metrics.definition: area under response-rate accuracy curve using MSP

baselines: AugMix, Cutout, MoEx, Mixup, CutMix, Style Transfer, adversarial training
eval.protocol: single evaluation per model; no seeds or significance tests stated

results.claim: FID between ImageNet-A and ImageNet validation set is 50.40, versus about 0.99 between ImageNet val and test.
Graduate-student human accuracy on ImageNet-A is about 90%.
ImageNet-A: 81,413 dragonfly images downloaded, 8,925 after ResNet-50 filter, 1,452 after diversified shortlist, 80 hand-selected.
Maximum Logit detector does not beat MSP across over 10 models (DenseNet-121 AUPR 16.1 to 15.8).
DeVries confidence branch gets 14.3% AUPR, about 2 points below MSP.
ImageNet-A and ImageNet-O sizes: 7,500 and 2,000 images.
Random-chance AUPR on ImageNet-O is about 16.67%.
Engstrom et al. estimate ImageNetV2 drop is under 3.6%; ImageNet-A accuracy can fall by over 50%.

limits: Filtered only against ResNet-50 so the set is biased to that model's errors; transfer shown empirically.
Trained-model runs report one number each, no seeds or intervals; training hyperparameters of the augmentation runs not given.
Vision only; ImageNet-O gains from ImageNet-21K are discounted because of image overlap.
Authors suggest not training on ImageNet-22K for ImageNet-O since it becomes trivial.
Table 1 prints DeiT-small 19.1 while text says 19.0.
